html:
The Bribri are an Indigenous people of the Talamanca mountains and valleys of southeastern Costa Rica and of northwestern Panama. They speak Bribri, a Chibchan language, and by some counts number up to about 35,000. Clans pass through the mother, and land is inherited through women.

They farm in the forest, growing cacao, plantains and other crops, and cacao has a sacred place in their beliefs. Their awá healers keep long chanted traditions.

The mountains of Talamanca protected them from the Spanish. Missionaries came and went, and in 1709 the Bribri and Cabécar rose and killed missionaries and soldiers under the leader Pablo Presbere, who was captured and executed in 1710. Talamanca stayed largely outside Spanish control. Neighbours: Huetar and Teribe.
